title: Canary scheduling and rollback ownership handoff - Novacore POC weekly
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on finalizing canary schedule, rollback ownership, runbook responsibilities, monitoring thresholds and a staging dry-run. Redwood AE/SE clarified canary timing, telemetry gating, and automation for rollback; Novacore asked about private deployment behaviors, audit logs, and who will own on-call handoffs during cutover. Agreed to run a full dry-run in staging Friday, Redwood to share runbook and telemetry thresholds, customer to validate SLOs and update on-call rotations.
topics: Staging dry-run schedule and success criteria
next_steps: Redwood to send updated canary runbook (link + PDF) by EOD Jan 13
Novacore SRE to verify alert thresholds and confirm SLO owners by Jan 14
Schedule full staging dry-run Friday Jan 15 09:00-10:30 PT
SE to provide dedicated capacity cost estimate if committed by Jan 20
Set 30-min post-dry-run retrospective slot Jan 15 11:00 PT
action_items: Priya Menon | Share canary runbook + incident playbook, include link to runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/novacore-canary-v1 | 2027-01-13
Ethan Zhou | Prepare a staging traffic generator script and small chaos test plan | 2027-01-14
Lena Ortiz | Validate alert thresholds and confirm SLO owners in PagerDuty | 2027-01-14
Derek Hale | Confirm rollback owner and on-call rotation for cutover window | 2027-01-14
Maya Green | Book retrospective and add runbook reviewers to calendar invite | 2027-01-13
transcript:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): Okay everyone, thanks for jumping on. quick agenda: canary schedule, rollback ownership, runbook handoff, and the staging dry run on Friday. um, Ethan will walk through the automation bits.
[00:18] Sita (Novacore): Sounds good. we have Derek and Lena here to speak to ops and the on-call rotations.
[00:28] Ethan (Redwood SE): Hey team, so, last week's telemetry looked pretty healthy - prefix hits up, latency p95 around 220-240ms on our test traffic. note that the p95 spikes were correlated with a few long tail requests from a specific user bucket - probable prompt length variance.
[00:46] Derek: got it. can you remind me again what the KV cache behavior is during a canary? we run a mixed sequence length workload and want to avoid cold-start penalties.
[00:54] Ethan: yeah, good point. our runtime keeps per-instance KV cache warm for active sessions, but during canary ramp we recommend sticky sessions for the first 5 minutes at each traffic step, otherwise you see kv cache misses and token latency increases. it's in the runbook section 2, but we flagged it here.
[01:12] Lena: when you say sticky, are you suggesting session affinity at the LB level? we don't want to change our infra too much.
[01:20] Ethan: You can do it at load balancer or at the request router in Redwood - simplest is an edge cookie affinity for canary buckets. we can also do a short-lived warmup batch to populate kv cache before traffic cutover.
[01:33] Sita: How long is the canary ramp again? I recall proposals of 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over a few hours, but that feels slow for our launch window.
[01:42] Priya: Right; proposed default: 1% for 15 minutes, 5% for 30 minutes, 25% for 45 minutes, then 100% after 30 minutes if all gates pass. But we're flexible - Derek, what does your ops window allow?
[01:55] Derek: For this release we have a two-hour quiet window. we can compress: 1% 10m, 5% 20m, 25% 30m, then decision. Need gating criteria spelled out though.
[02:05] Priya: Totally. gating criteria: p50/p95 latency within X% of baseline, error rate below 0.2% for 5 minutes, and no SSO/auth regressions. We'll put precise thresholds in the runbook.
[02:18] Lena: On alerts - we want Prometheus + Grafana alerts wired and a PagerDuty mapping. will Redwood push alerts or do we?
[02:26] Ethan: Redwood will provide recommended alert definitions and a Grafana dashboard export; we do not push directly into your PagerDuty. we can provide a YAML for your alertmanager.
[02:36] Omar: what about audit logs and retention for the private control plane? Security wants 1 year of tamper-evident logs.
[02:44] Maya (CSM): We have a SOC2+ option for Private and Dedicated customers - audit logs can be exported to your S3/KMS with retention policy. I'll attach the security brief.
[02:56] Sita: Good. Rollback question — who hits the button? automated rollback on threshold breaches or manual?
[03:03] Ethan: Our platform supports automated rollback when a gate trips, but customers usually opt for manual approval for high-risk launches. For this POC we suggest automated rollback to a pinned previous model if latency or errors exceed thresholds, with a required manual confirmation to reattempt cutover.
[03:20] Derek: We want clear ownership — Novacore infra team to own rollback execution, Redwood to own model fallback and support for automation. That sound right?
[03:28] Priya: Yes. propose: Novacore is primary rollback executor (they have final network control), Redwood provides the fallback image and automation scripts and will standby during the window. We'll add contact matrix in runbook.
[03:40] Lena: okay who's on-call for immediate post-failure investigation?
[03:44] Priya: Redwood SE (Ethan) stands by for first-responder model/runtime issues for the window; Novacore SRE handles network and infra. We'll make a three-way escalation in the playbook.
[03:58] Sita: can we see a sample incident playbook?
[04:02] Priya: Yes — attached in the runbook link, and we'll pdf it.
[04:08] Ethan: Quick note on canary traffic shaping — recommend using randomized bucket selection to avoid correlated user behavior, and apply a small synthetic validation set injected at 0.1% to validate output quality.
[04:22] Derek: How do we verify output quality? we need a door hang of automated evals and a manual sampling step.
[04:28] Maya: Redwood can run a parallel evaluation using our eval harness and we'll surface regression alerts. We'll include an eval set and the failure definitions.
[04:35] Sita: Ok. Regarding the staging dry-run Friday — what's the success criteria?
[04:40] Priya: Success criteria: 1) canary ramp script runs without incident, 2) KV cache warmup reduces p95 by expected delta, 3) alerts fire correctly and map into PagerDuty, 4) automated rollback simulation successfully restores previous model state.
[04:53] Lena: and we want an end-to-end user path smoke test too — login, inference, and audit log capture.
[04:59] Ethan: We'll include that in the generator script. Also small chaos: kill one pod mid-ramp and ensure fallback behaves.
[05:09] Derek: Can we compress the schedule so user traffic reaches 100% within the 2-hour quiet window?
[05:14] Priya: Yes, compressing is fine, we'll update the durations. We'll surface estimated risk levels for each compression step.
[05:22] Sita: One more question: dedicated capacity — if we switch to Dedicated right after POC, how fast can Redwood provision and what are the cost levers?
[05:30] Priya: Dedicated provisioning lead time depends on region and GPU type; typical in-region provisioning is 2-4 weeks for initial pool. Cost levers include batching, quantization profiles, and KV cache hit improvements — we'll put a cost-savings estimate in the cost sheet.
[05:42] Derek: please include a per-hour estimate for the canary window so we can align budget owners.
[05:47] Priya: Will do.
[05:49] Sita: Anything else?
[05:51] Priya: Final recap — Redwood to share runbook and links, SE to prepare staging scripts, Novacore to validate alerts and on-call rotations, schedule dry-run Friday, post-dry-run retro. Thanks all.
[06:03] (end of recording)
notes: Runbook link: https://redwood.app/runbooks/novacore-canary-v1 (Redwood will update with compressed schedule)
Security brief and SOC2 export options attached by Maya (CSM)
Staging dry-run scheduled Jan 15 09:00-10:30 PT - invite to follow
